title: Zomato Starts Charging Up to Rs 20 on Cash-on-Delivery Orders
excerpt: The 'pay on delivery fee' appears as a separate line in the bill summary on cash orders, on top of platform fees, packaging charges and GST — while online payments remain exempt.
body:
• Zomato has begun adding a separate "pay on delivery fee" of Rs 5 to Rs 20 on orders where customers choose cash on delivery, visible in the app's bill summary since September 12.
  • The charge is separate from the platform fee, packaging charges and GST, and customers who pay online do not incur it.
  • The move follows a March increase in Zomato's platform fee to Rs 14.99 per order and an August round of layoffs affecting about 250 employees.
  • With 2.3 to 2.5 million orders processed daily, even small per-order fees can scale into hundreds of crores in annual revenue — and rival Swiggy has not yet introduced a similar charge.

Paying cash for your Zomato order just got more expensive. The food delivery platform, backed by Eternal, has started adding a separate "pay on delivery fee" to orders where customers opt to pay in cash when the food arrives. App listings reviewed by Moneycontrol show the charge appearing as its own line in the bill summary, typically at Rs 5, though some users have been billed Rs 7 and, in certain cases, as much as Rs 20.

What Customers Are Seeing

The new fee began appearing on Saturday, September 12, according to multiple reports. It is listed separately from Zomato's platform fee, restaurant packaging charges and applicable GST. Customers who pay online — via UPI, net banking or cards — do not see the charge.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=zeCOnb_34nk

The amount does not appear to be uniform. Moneycontrol reported instances of Rs 7 and up to Rs 20 on some orders, and the Economic Times has separately reported the fee can go as high as Rs 30 in some cases, suggesting the charge may vary by order or customer rather than being a flat levy. Zomato has not publicly explained how the amount is set or where the charge has been rolled out.

Why Now

The fee is the latest move in a steady monetisation of the ordering process. Zomato processes an estimated 2.3 to 2.5 million food orders a day. At that scale, even a Rs 5 charge on cash orders alone could add meaningfully to revenue — one estimate put the theoretical upper bound at Rs 1.15 to Rs 1.25 crore per day, or Rs 420 to Rs 456 crore annually, though cash-on-delivery orders make up only a portion of total volumes.

The move also comes amid intensifying competition. Rapido's Ownly is gaining traction in food delivery, and Flipkart is piloting its Eat In offering — squeezing the margins of the two incumbents and pushing them to find new revenue lines.

A History of Adding Fees

Food-delivery platforms began introducing platform fees in April 2023, with Swiggy testing a Rs 2 charge and Zomato following suit. Zomato raised its platform fee earlier this year from Rs 12.50 to Rs 14.99 per order, with GST charged separately — taking the effective charge to Rs 17.58 per order, according to Moneycontrol. The new cash-on-delivery fee sits on top of all of that.

So far, rival Swiggy has not introduced an equivalent cash-handling charge, according to IANS. Whether it follows suit will be watched closely, since the two companies have tended to move in lockstep on fees.

Cost-Cutting Backdrop

The fee arrives weeks after Zomato laid off around 250 employees in a restructuring reported in August. The cuts followed a review of the company's customer-delight operating model, and the company discontinued its Customer Delight operations in Hyderabad, consolidating its remaining in-house customer service at a single location in Gurgaon.

Taken together, the fee hikes and the staff cuts point to a push to improve unit economics in a market where growth has slowed and competition has sharpened.

What to Watch

Journalists have contacted Zomato for clarification, but the company has not yet issued a public explanation of the fee. Watch for whether Swiggy introduces its own version, whether consumer complaints push regulators to scrutinise cash-handling charges, and whether the fee nudges more customers toward digital payments — which may be the point.

nri_angle: NRIs ordering food for family back in India — and anyone watching India's delivery duopoly — now see another line item on the bill, with cash-paying customers bearing the cost.
